title: Simplicial latching colimits identify naturally with degenerate subsets
statement: Let $T:\Delta^{\mathrm{op}}\to\mathrm{Sets}$ be a small simplicial set [def-weil-pbc-simplicial-set] and $n\geq0$. Let $\mathcal L_n$ have as objects the surjective order-preserving maps $\sigma:[n]\twoheadrightarrow[k]$ with $k<n$. A morphism from $\sigma$ to $\sigma'$ is a surjection $\rho:[k']\twoheadrightarrow[k]$ satisfying $\sigma=\rho\sigma'$. Form the diagram $\sigma\mapsto T_k$, $\rho\mapsto T(\rho):T_k\to T_{k'}$, and its colimit $L_nT$ in sets [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit]. The canonical map $\lambda_n:L_nT\to T_n$ induced by the $T(\sigma)$ is injective with image exactly $D_nT$, the set of degenerate $n$-simplices. Thus $L_nT\cong D_nT$, with the colimit structure map at $\sigma$ given by $T(\sigma)$ valued in $D_nT$. These identifications are natural under all maps of simplicial sets $T\to T'$, where $D_nT\to D_nT'$ is their restriction to the degenerate subsets. When $n=0$, both $L_0T$ and $D_0T$ are empty.

source.place: Tag 017R, lemma-splitting-simplicial-sets, statement and proof; consequence for the proper-surjection colimit. This colimit identification is the auxiliary latching calculation in Joyal–Tierney Section 2, Theorem 2.6 and Proposition 2.10, expanded by the agent rather than asserted as the literal statement of 017R.

proof.text: The indexing category is finite: there are finitely many $k<n$ and finitely many order-preserving maps between any two of these finite ordinals. Identities and composition are those of the indicated surjections, with the direction specified in the statement. Functoriality of $T$ [def-weil-pbc-simplicial-set] gives the diagram and a cocone $j_\sigma:T_k\to D_nT$, $j_\sigma(y)=T(\sigma)y$: these values are degenerate since $k<n$. For an arrow $\sigma\to\sigma'$ represented by $\rho$ with $\sigma=\rho\circ\sigma'$, one has $j_{\sigma'}T(\rho)=T(\sigma')T(\rho)=T(\sigma)=j_\sigma$. We will verify the universal property [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit] of this cocone directly, thus also proving existence of the set colimit without appealing to a separate colimit-existence theorem.

source.place: Tag 017R (lemma-splitting-simplicial-sets), agent expansion to the proper-surjection cocone; colimit means Stacks Tag 002F (categories.tex, definition-colimit).

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-simplicial-set-nondegenerate-decomposition] to every simplex: its normal form is $x=T(\tau)z$ with $\tau:[n]\twoheadrightarrow[r]$ and $z\in T_r$ nondegenerate, and the entire triple $(r,\tau,z)$ is unique. If $x\in D_nT$, this normal form has $r<n$. Indeed, by [def-weil-pbc-simplicial-set], write $x=T(f)y$ with $f:[n]\to[m]$, $m<n$. List the nonempty image of $f$ increasingly as the image of $i:[a]\hookrightarrow[m]$, and let $e:[n]\twoheadrightarrow[a]$ send an element to the index of its image; then $f=i\circ e$ and $a\le m<n$. Apply the same decomposition theorem to $T(i)y\in T_a$, writing it as $T(\eta)z'$ for a surjection $\eta:[a]\twoheadrightarrow[b]$. Since $b\le a$, the expression $x=T(\eta\circ e)z'$ has $b<n$; uniqueness identifies it with $(r,\tau,z)$. Conversely, a normal form with $r<n$ is degenerate by definition. Thus for every element of $D_nT$ its unique normal-form surjection is an object of $\mathcal L_n$.

source.place: Tag 017R (lemma-splitting-simplicial-sets), existence and uniqueness of the splitting; image enumeration and the dimension bound written out by the agent.

proof.text:
Let $(M,(c_\sigma))$ be any cocone on the diagram, so $c_{\sigma'}T(\rho)=c_\sigma$ for the arrows in the statement [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit]. For $x\in D_nT$ with the unique normal form $(r,\tau,z)$ of step 2, define $h(x)=c_\tau(z)$; uniqueness makes this unambiguous. To prove its factorization equation on the whole of each $T_k$, take $\sigma:[n]\twoheadrightarrow[k]$, $k<n$, and arbitrary $y\in T_k$. By [lem-weil-pbc-simplicial-set-nondegenerate-decomposition], write $y=T(\rho)z$ with $\rho:[k]\twoheadrightarrow[r]$ and $z$ nondegenerate. Then $r\le k<n$ and $j_\sigma(y)=T(\rho\circ\sigma)z$. Uniqueness identifies this as its normal form. Put $\tau=\rho\circ\sigma$; the map $\rho$ is an arrow $\tau\to\sigma$ of $\mathcal L_n$. Therefore
$$h(j_\sigma(y))=c_\tau(z)=c_\sigma(T(\rho)z)=c_\sigma(y).$$
This includes $\rho=\mathrm{id}$ when $y$ is already nondegenerate.

source.place: Tag 017R (lemma-splitting-simplicial-sets), agent construction of descent using unique normal forms; Tag 002F (categories.tex, definition-colimit), cocone equation.

proof.text: The factorization in step 3 is unique. If $h':D_nT\to M$ also satisfies $h'j_\sigma=c_\sigma$ for every $\sigma$, take the normal form $x=T(\tau)z$ from step 2. Since $\tau$ is an object of $\mathcal L_n$, $h'(x)=h'(j_\tau(z))=c_\tau(z)=h(x)$. Hence $(D_nT,(j_\sigma))$ is a colimit by [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit]. When $n=0$ there are no $k<0$ and no degenerate simplices [def-weil-pbc-simplicial-set]; the same universal property is the uniqueness of the function from the empty set to $M$. This proves the empty-degree case as well.

source.place: Tag 017R (lemma-splitting-simplicial-sets), agent uniqueness argument; Tag 002F (categories.tex, definition-colimit), including the empty diagram.

proof.text: Compare this colimit with any chosen $L_nT$ [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit]. Let $\iota_\sigma:T_k\to L_nT$ be its structure maps. The two universal properties give maps $a_T:L_nT\to D_nT$ and $b_T:D_nT\to L_nT$ with $a_T\iota_\sigma=j_\sigma$ and $b_Tj_\sigma=\iota_\sigma$. Their composites have the same composites with all structure maps as the corresponding identities, so uniqueness in each universal property gives $b_Ta_T=\mathrm{id}$ and $a_Tb_T=\mathrm{id}$. If $u_T:D_nT\hookrightarrow T_n$ is the subset inclusion, then $u_Ta_T\iota_\sigma=T(\sigma)$, so $u_Ta_T=\lambda_n$ by uniqueness. Since $a_T$ is bijective and $u_T$ is injective, $\lambda_n$ is injective and its image is exactly $D_nT$. The equation $a_T\iota_\sigma=j_\sigma$ gives precisely the requested structure maps.

source.place: Tag 017R (lemma-splitting-simplicial-sets), agent comparison of the two colimit cocones; Tag 002F (categories.tex, definition-colimit), uniqueness up to unique isomorphism.

proof.text:
For any simplicial map $\phi:T\to T'$, naturality [def-weil-pbc-simplicial-set] gives
$$\phi_n(T(\sigma)y)=T'(\sigma)(\phi_k(y)).$$
This is degenerate whenever $k<n$, so by step 2 $\phi_n$ restricts to a map $d_\phi:D_nT\to D_nT'$, and $d_\phi j_\sigma=j'_\sigma\phi_k$. The same naturality equation makes the $\phi_k$ a map of the latching diagrams; its induced map $L_n\phi$ satisfies $L_n\phi\,\iota_\sigma=\iota'_\sigma\phi_k$ [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit]. Consequently $a_{T'}L_n\phi$ and $d_\phi a_T$ agree after every $\iota_\sigma$, both with value $j'_\sigma\phi_k$, and the colimit uniqueness gives $a_{T'}L_n\phi=d_\phi a_T$. Restrictions of identity maps and composites are identities and composites, so this is naturality under all simplicial maps, also for the empty sets in degree zero.

lean.statement: theorem simplicialLatchingMap_spec {T T' : SSet.{u}} (n : ℕ) : Function.Injective (latchingTo T n) ∧ Set.range (latchingTo T n) = T.degenerate n ∧ (∀ (σ : LatchingIndex n) (x : T _⦋σ.unop.obj.right.len⦌), latchingTo T n (colimit.ι (latchingDiagram T n) σ x) = T.map σ.unop.obj.hom.op x) ∧ (∀ (φ : T ⟶ T'), φ.app (Opposite.op ⦋n⦌) ∘ latchingTo T n = latchingTo T' n ∘ latchingMap φ n) ∧ (∀ (φ : T ⟶ T'), Set.MapsTo (φ.app (Opposite.op ⦋n⦌)) (T.degenerate n) (T'.degenerate n)) ∧ (n = 0 → IsEmpty (LatchingIndex n) ∧ IsEmpty (latching T n) ∧ IsEmpty (T.degenerate n))
